title: Card surcharges limited to the cost of acceptance
summary: Card surcharges above the merchant's cost of acceptance were banned for large merchants from 1 September 2016 and for all other merchants from 1 September 2017.

instruments.title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Payment Surcharges) Act 2016
RBA Standard No. 3 of 2016 (Scheme Rules relating to Merchant Pricing)

direction_rationale: Limiting surcharges to cost stops merchants using card fees as a hidden margin, sharpening price comparison.
comparison: Large merchants (two of: revenue of $25m or more, assets of $12.5m or more, 50 or more staff) versus others during the year between the two dates
notes: Needs firm-level data for the merchant-size design.

'alicia dates' reports 'differs': the Act commenced on assent (25 February 2016); the RBA standard made under it applied to large merchants from 1 September 2016, which is the effective date used.

assessment.summary: Card surcharges may not exceed what accepting the card costs the merchant. Prices become clearer and surcharges can no longer be a hidden margin.

marks.reason: Surcharges must reflect the cost of card acceptance.
Stops excessive surcharges being used as a hidden margin, making prices easier to compare.

responsible.note: Administers the Payment Systems (Regulation) Act 1998 and the Competition and Consumer Act 2010.

history.what: Surcharges banned on eftpos, Mastercard and Visa payments, with lower interchange caps.
